drugs.name: amoxicillin–clavulanate
drugs.notes: Dose is total product (amoxicillin + clavulanate). ISCAID UTI 2019 Table 3: 12.5–25 mg/kg PO q12h dogs/cats (sporadic cystitis; no proven advantage over plain amoxicillin). ISCAID respiratory 2017: dogs 11 mg/kg PO q12h; cats 12.5 mg/kg PO q12h (combination). ISCAID canine pyoderma 2025 first-choice: 12.5 mg/kg PO q12h (higher anecdotal doses: evidence lacking).
drugs.source: ISCAID UTI guidelines (Weese et al. Vet J 2019;247:8–25) Table 3 DOI 10.1016/j.tvjl.2019.02.008; ISCAID respiratory (Lappin et al. JVIM 2017) Table 2 DOI 10.1111/jvim.14627 PMC5354050; ISCAID canine pyoderma (Loeffler et al. Vet Dermatol 2025) DOI 10.1111/vde.13342

drugs.name: doxycycline
drugs.notes: ISCAID respiratory 2017 Table 2: 5 mg/kg PO q12h or 10 mg/kg PO q24h (URI/CIRDC/bronchitis; Chlamydia/Mycoplasma/Bordetella). Same regimen in ISCAID pyoderma 2025 (second-choice; BC/AST for specific drug). Cats: follow PO tablets/capsules with water/food to reduce esophageal stricture risk (guideline narrative). Frequency: 5 mg/kg q12h OR 10 mg/kg q24h.
drugs.source: ISCAID respiratory guidelines (Lappin et al. JVIM 2017) Table 2 DOI 10.1111/jvim.14627 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5354050/; ISCAID canine pyoderma 2025 DOI 10.1111/vde.13342

drugs.name: enrofloxacin (dog)
drugs.notes: Dogs 5–20 mg/kg PO/IM/IV q24h (ISCAID respiratory 2017 Table 2; ISCAID UTI 2019 Table 3). Pyoderma 2025: 5–20 mg/kg PO q24h; minimum 10 mg/kg for staphylococci; 20 mg/kg for Pseudomonas. Reserve fluoroquinolone; BC/AST preferred. Frequency: q24h.
drugs.source: ISCAID respiratory (Lappin et al. JVIM 2017) Table 2 DOI 10.1111/jvim.14627 PMC5354050; ISCAID UTI (Weese et al. Vet J 2019) Table 3 DOI 10.1016/j.tvjl.2019.02.008; ISCAID canine pyoderma 2025 DOI 10.1111/vde.13342

drugs.name: enrofloxacin (cat)
drugs.notes: Cats ≤5 mg/kg/day — do not exceed (retinal degeneration risk). ISCAID respiratory 2017 Table 2: Cats 5 mg/kg PO q24h; ISCAID UTI 2019 Table 3: 5 mg/kg PO every 24 h (cats). Reserve fluoroquinolone; BC/AST preferred. Frequency: q24h.
drugs.source: ISCAID respiratory (Lappin et al. JVIM 2017) Table 2 DOI 10.1111/jvim.14627 PMC5354050; ISCAID UTI (Weese et al. Vet J 2019) Table 3 DOI 10.1016/j.tvjl.2019.02.008; ISCAID canine pyoderma 2025 DOI 10.1111/vde.13342

drugs.name: cefovecin
drugs.frequency: once; dogs may repeat once if incomplete response (max 2 injections); cats single one-time injection per FDA label
drugs.notes: FDA/EMA label: 8 mg/kg (3.6 mg/lb) SC. Dogs: one injection; second 8 mg/kg SC if incomplete response; maximum two injections. Cats: single one-time SC injection. Reconstituted 80 mg/mL. ISCAID respiratory 2017 also lists 8 mg/kg SC once, may repeat after 7–14 days (extra-label URI context). ISCAID UTI: only if oral not possible. ISCAID pyoderma 2025: second-choice 8 mg/kg SC once; may repeat after 14 days with BC/AST. Frequency: once; dogs may repeat once if incomplete response (max 2 injections); cats single one-time injection per FDA label.
drugs.source: FDA DailyMed CONVENIA (cefovecin sodium) label https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=2daeaf25-f98f-49d3-943c-f604a844d93c; 21 CFR 522.311; ISCAID respiratory JVIM 2017 Table 2 DOI 10.1111/jvim.14627

drugs.name: maropitant (injectable)
drugs.frequency: q24h (injectable up to 5 consecutive days per label)
drugs.notes: Injectable Cerenia: dogs and cats ≥4 months 1 mg/kg IV (over 1–2 min) or SC once daily up to 5 days; dogs 2–4 months SC only at 1 mg/kg. Injectable 10 mg/mL. iCatCare CKD 2026 cats: maropitant 1 mg/kg SC, IV or PO q24h (nausea/vomiting). ACVIM pancreatitis cats 2021 names maropitant as preferred antiemetic but does not state mg/kg in main text. Frequency: q24h (injectable up to 5 consecutive days per label).
drugs.source: FDA DailyMed CERENIA (maropitant citrate) Injectable https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=6aeda328-97c9-4868-8ecb-b3a4dcdbc0a0; Zoetis Cerenia tablets/injectable package insert; iCatCare CKD cats 2026 (Taylor et al. JFMS 2026) Table 4 DOI 10.1177/1098612X261466553

drugs.name: maropitant (tablet, acute vomiting)
drugs.notes: FDA Cerenia tablets (dogs only): minimum 2 mg/kg PO once daily for acute vomiting prevention. Tablet strengths 16/24/60/160 mg. Not interchangeable with injectable for motion sickness. Frequency: q24h (acute vomiting prevention).
drugs.source: FDA DailyMed CERENIA (maropitant citrate) Injectable https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=6aeda328-97c9-4868-8ecb-b3a4dcdbc0a0; Zoetis Cerenia tablets/injectable package insert; iCatCare CKD cats 2026 (Taylor et al. JFMS 2026) Table 4 DOI 10.1177/1098612X261466553

drugs.name: maropitant (tablet, motion sickness)
drugs.notes: FDA Cerenia tablets: motion sickness dogs ≥4 months minimum 8 mg/kg PO once daily up to 2 days. Tablet strengths 16/24/60/160 mg. Not interchangeable with injectable for motion sickness. Frequency: q24h up to 2 days (motion sickness).
drugs.source: FDA DailyMed CERENIA (maropitant citrate) Injectable https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=6aeda328-97c9-4868-8ecb-b3a4dcdbc0a0; Zoetis Cerenia tablets/injectable package insert; iCatCare CKD cats 2026 (Taylor et al. JFMS 2026) Table 4 DOI 10.1177/1098612X261466553

drugs.name: ondansetron
drugs.notes: iCatCare CKD 2026 Table 4 (cats): 0.1–1 mg/kg IV (slowly), IM, SC or PO q6–12h; SC higher bioavailability; use higher end orally. Extra-label. ACVIM pancreatitis cats 2021 endorses ondansetron ± maropitant combination but main text lacks mg/kg. Dog-specific consensus mg/kg not locked from priority guidelines in this pass.
drugs.source: iCatCare consensus CKD cats 2026 (Taylor et al. J Feline Med Surg 2026) Table 4 DOI 10.1177/1098612X261466553

drugs.name: famotidine
drugs.frequency: q12h (study regimens; one gastritis study used 0.5 mg/kg q24h)
drugs.notes: NOT a panel-endorsed first-line equal to PPI. ACVIM GI protectants 2018 cites study doses: dogs famotidine 0.5 mg/kg q12h (beagles) or 1–1.3 mg/kg q12h (mixed-breed; weak pH effect); cats 0.88–1.26 mg/kg PO q12h (inferior to omeprazole). Tachyphylaxis within days. Consensus: twice-daily H2RA monotherapy inferior to twice-daily PPI; do not combine H2RA with PPI. iCatCare CKD 2026 prefers omeprazole over famotidine for suspected ulceration. Frequency: q12h (study regimens; one gastritis study used 0.5 mg/kg q24h).
drugs.source: ACVIM consensus GI protectants (Marks et al. JVIM 2018;32:1823–1840) DOI 10.1111/jvim.15337 PMC6271318 (study doses cited in H2RA clinical efficacy section)

drugs.name: omeprazole
drugs.notes: 1 mg/kg PO q12h is from iCatCare CKD 2026 (cats, strongly suspected/proven gastroduodenal ulceration) and AAHA anesthesia 2020 (peri-op GER-risk: 1 mg/kg at least twice — evening prior and morning of anesthesia). ACVIM GI protectants 2018 prefer PPI twice daily for acid-related GUE but do not state a single universal mg/kg; taper after ≥3–4 weeks continuous use. Extra-label in dogs/cats. Frequency: q12h.
drugs.source: iCatCare CKD cats 2026 Table 4 DOI 10.1177/1098612X261466553; 2020 AAHA Anesthesia and Monitoring Guidelines (Grubb et al.) DOI 10.5326/JAAHA-MS-7055; ACVIM GI protectants Marks et al. JVIM 2018 DOI 10.1111/jvim.15337

drugs.name: prednisolone
drugs.notes: Multiple indication-specific regimens. ISCAID pyoderma 2025 (dogs, pyotraumatic adjunct): prednisolone 0.5–1.0 mg/kg PO once daily for 5–7 days. ACVIM pancreatitis cats 2021 (chronic; panel split): anti-inflammatory 0.5–1.0 mg/kg PO q24h tapering OR immunosuppressive 2.0 mg/kg q12h × 5 d then 1.0 mg/kg q12h × 6 weeks then taper (close monitoring). Prednisone often used interchangeably in dogs; cats typically prednisolone. Dose entry above reflects common anti-inflammatory range; immunosuppressive chronic pancreatitis regimen is higher — see notes. Frequency: q24h (anti-inflammatory adjunct regimens below).
drugs.source: ISCAID canine pyoderma 2025 (Loeffler et al. Vet Dermatol 2025) DOI 10.1111/vde.13342; ACVIM pancreatitis cats (Forman et al. JVIM 2021;35:703–723) DOI 10.1111/jvim.16053 PMC7995362

drugs.name: meloxicam (dog)
drugs.frequency: load then q24h maintenance — see notes
drugs.notes: Dogs (FDA Metacam): load 0.2 mg/kg IV or SC once on day 1, then maintenance 0.1 mg/kg PO q24h. Injectable 5 mg/mL common. dosePerKg field spans load 0.2 and maintenance 0.1. Frequency: load then q24h maintenance — see notes.
drugs.source: FDA/eCFR 21 CFR 522.1367 meloxicam; DailyMed METACAM injection; ISFM acute pain cats 2022 (Steagall et al. JFMS 2022;24:4–30) Table 7 DOI 10.1177/1098612X211066268

drugs.name: meloxicam (cat, US label)
drugs.notes: US FDA injectable boxed warning: 0.3 mg/kg SC once only before orthopedic/OVH/castration; do NOT repeat injectable or follow with oral meloxicam/other NSAIDs (repeated use associated with acute renal failure and death). Do not use IV in cats. ISFM lower regimens (notes only, not encoded in dosePerKg): panel-preferred 0.2 mg/kg SC once then 0.05 mg/kg PO q24h × 4 days; EU chronic 0.1 mg/kg PO day 1 then 0.05 mg/kg PO q24h. Injectable 5 mg/mL common. Frequency: once only (US FDA injectable).
drugs.source: FDA/eCFR 21 CFR 522.1367 meloxicam; DailyMed METACAM injection; ISFM acute pain cats 2022 (Steagall et al. JFMS 2022;24:4–30) Table 7 DOI 10.1177/1098612X211066268

drugs.name: gabapentin
drugs.frequency: q8h (neuropathic pain minimum per AAHA anesthesia 2020)
drugs.notes: AAHA Anesthesia 2020 neuropathic pain MINIMUM only: gabapentin minimum 10 mg/kg q8h for pre-existing neuropathic pain; unlikely to provide analgesia for acute inflammatory pain — not a complete analgesic formulary entry. 2022 AAHA Pain discusses gabapentin as adjunct but does not state mg/kg in main text. iCatCare CKD 2026: CKD cats — regimens for gabapentinoids not established for analgesia; for pre-visit anxiolysis example 'up to 10 mg/kg, with 25–50 mg usually adequate as a total dose' due to accumulation. Extra-label. Frequency: q8h (neuropathic pain minimum per AAHA anesthesia 2020).
drugs.source: 2020 AAHA Anesthesia and Monitoring Guidelines (Grubb et al.) DOI 10.5326/JAAHA-MS-7055; iCatCare CKD cats 2026 DOI 10.1177/1098612X261466553 (CKD anxiolysis note)

drugs.name: buprenorphine
drugs.frequency: up to q8h (standard concentration); high-concentration SC product up to 24 h
drugs.notes: ISFM acute pain cats 2022 Table 6: standard 0.3 mg/mL product 0.02–0.04 mg/kg IV, IM or OTM up to 8 h (mild–moderate pain); SC with standard formulation not recommended. High-concentration 1.8 mg/mL (Simbadol-type): 0.24 mg/kg SC up to 24 h. ACVIM MMVD dogs (sedation combo with acepromazine): buprenorphine 0.0075–0.01 mg/kg IV/IM/SC as needed — dog entry context, not feline analgesic range. Frequency: up to q8h (standard concentration); high-concentration SC product up to 24 h.
drugs.source: ISFM Consensus Guidelines Acute Pain in Cats 2022 (Steagall et al. JFMS 2022;24:4–30) Table 6 DOI 10.1177/1098612X211066268; ACVIM MMVD dogs 2019 (Keene et al. JVIM 2019) DOI 10.1111/jvim.15488 (dog sedation combo only)

drugs.name: butorphanol (cat)
drugs.notes: ISFM acute pain cats 2022 Table 6: analgesia 0.2–0.4 mg/kg IV or IM for 1–2 h (mild pain/sedation facilitation); does NOT provide adequate analgesia as sole analgesic for routine surgery. Reversal of pure agonists: 0.02–0.05 mg/kg IV only. Frequency: q1–2h (analgesia duration short).
drugs.source: ISFM acute pain cats 2022 Table 6 DOI 10.1177/1098612X211066268

drugs.name: butorphanol (dog)
drugs.frequency: as needed (ACVIM MMVD acute CHF sedation)
drugs.notes: ACVIM MMVD dogs 2019: butorphanol 0.2–0.25 mg/kg IM or IV as needed for anxiety/dyspnea sedation in acute CHF. Frequency: as needed (ACVIM MMVD acute CHF sedation).
drugs.source: ACVIM MMVD (Keene et al. JVIM 2019;33:1127–1140) DOI 10.1111/jvim.15488 PMC6524084

drugs.name: acepromazine
drugs.notes: ACVIM MMVD 2019: with buprenorphine 0.0075–0.01 mg/kg, acepromazine 0.01–0.03 mg/kg IV, IM or SC as needed for alternative sedation in acute dyspnea (monitor BP/respiration). Context-limited (acute CHF); not a general premedication formulary from this source alone. Cat-specific consensus mg/kg not locked here. Frequency: as needed (acute CHF sedation context).
drugs.source: ACVIM consensus MMVD dogs (Keene et al. JVIM 2019;33:1127–1140) DOI 10.1111/jvim.15488 PMC6524084

drugs.name: furosemide
drugs.frequency: acute: boluses; chronic: commonly q12h PO — see notes
drugs.notes: ACVIM MMVD 2019 dogs: Acute Stage C — 2 mg/kg IV or IM then 2 mg/kg hourly until improved or total 8 mg/kg over 4 h; CRI 0.66–1 mg/kg/h after bolus if needed. Chronic Stage C — commonly ~2 mg/kg PO q12h (or as needed); ≥8 mg/kg/day despite standard Rx defines Stage D. Cat cardiomyopathy consensus names IV furosemide for acute CHF but numeric mg/kg not locked in this formulary pass from that page alone. Frequency: acute: boluses; chronic: commonly q12h PO — see notes.
drugs.source: ACVIM consensus MMVD dogs (Keene et al. JVIM 2019;33:1127–1140) DOI 10.1111/jvim.15488 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6524084/

drugs.name: pimobendan
drugs.notes: FDA Vetmedin label: total daily dose 0.5 mg/kg PO divided into 2 portions ~12 h apart (nearest half-tablet). ACVIM MMVD 2019: 0.25–0.3 mg/kg PO q12h for Stage B2 and Stage C; Stage D escalation off-label 0.3 mg/kg PO q8h. Dogs only on US label; contraindications include HCM/obstruction. Chewable tablets 1.25/2.5/5/10 mg. Frequency: q12h (total daily label 0.5 mg/kg divided ~q12h).
drugs.source: FDA DailyMed VETMEDIN (pimobendan) https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=5441e5b2-cdc0-477a-bd9a-ec5f8d912281; ACVIM MMVD Keene et al. JVIM 2019 DOI 10.1111/jvim.15488

drugs.name: methimazole

fixedTotal.note: FDA starting dose 2.5 mg q12h; not mg/kg

drugs.notes: FIXED DOSE (not mg/kg). FDA Felanorm start: 2.5 mg every 12 hours; after 3 weeks titrate in 2.5 mg increments based on TT4/clinical response; max 20 mg/day divided, no single dose >10 mg. Solution 5 mg/mL. Alternate starts (not encoded in fixedTotal): 2023 AAHA Selected Endocrinopathies — start 1.25–2.5 mg every 24 h week 1, then 2.5–5 mg every 12–24 h (staged titration). iCatCare CKD 2026 Box 9 for hyperthyroid IRIS 3–4: thiamazole 1 mg/cat q12h starting. Also called thiamazole. Frequency: q12h start; titrate after ~3 weeks.
drugs.source: FDA DailyMed FELANORM (methimazole) Oral Solution https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=2231391d-c118-42ee-9aa9-5dc6883bff9a; 2023 AAHA Selected Endocrinopathies (Bugbee et al.) DOI 10.5326/JAAHA-MS-7368; iCatCare CKD 2026 DOI 10.1177/1098612X261466553

drugs.name: insulin glargine (U-100)

fixedTotal.note: AAHA 2026: start most cats at 1 U/cat SC q12h; table allows 1–2 U/cat

drugs.notes: FIXED UNITS/CAT (not mg/kg). 2026 AAHA Diabetes Management Guidelines for Cats: glargine U-100 or PZI first choices — start most cats 1 U/cat SC every 12 h (Table 7.1 allows 1–2 U/cat); use lean/ideal weight if using any U/kg reasoning. Glargine U-300 separate: 0.5 U/kg lean BW SC q12–24h OR 2 U/cat SC q24h. NPH generally not acceptable in cats; lente not preferred first-line. Extra-label human insulin products common. Frequency: q12h.
drugs.source: 2026 AAHA Diabetes Management Guidelines for Cats (Bugbee et al. JAAHA 2026;62:65–93) DOI 10.5326/JAAHA-MS-7572 Table 7.1 / Sec 7
